title: The Inventory Rack
tagline: the second boss - many things under one name
hints: `std::vector<std::string> pack;` starts empty. `pack.push_back(item);` adds one to the end. `pack.size()` says how many.
Read with `while (std::getline(std::cin, line))` and `if (line == "done") break;` inside. getline gives you the whole line, spaces and all.
To print numbered items you need the index, so use a counting loop: `for (size_t i = 0; i < pack.size(); ++i)` and print `i + 1` as the human number.
To search, walk the vector with a range-for and set a bool: `for (const std::string& item : pack) { if (item == "torch") hasTorch = true; }`
`pack.back()` is the last element - but it crashes on an empty vector, which is exactly why the empty case is handled separately and returns early.
